scope: Bounded public terminology verification. Definitions only; no clinical advice, phenotype derivation, source-field recoding, or local clinical data transmitted.

patobank_ki67_percent.label: Ki-67 index (%)
patobank_ki67_percent.definition: Danish pathology code whose three-digit suffix gives the recorded Ki-67 index as an integer percentage from 0 through 100.
patobank_ki67_percent.mapping_rule: For an exact ÆKI followed by three digits with numeric value 0..100, the recorded percentage equals that suffix. Apply the same lookup to AEKI only through the atlas's documented Æ-to-AE normalization.
patobank_ki67_percent.verification: Patobank's full Ætiologi codebook explicitly enumerates all 101 rows ÆKI000 through ÆKI100 with matching percentages. Its breast-cancer coding guide separately explains the ÆKIxxx suffix rule.

locators.patobankEtiology: ÆKI000..ÆKI100; web text lines 1463..1563 as retrieved on verification date
locators.patobankBreastGuide: Printed page 4 (PDF page index 3), section Ki-67 proliferationsindex

caveats: The official code spelling uses Æ. AEKI is an atlas/export normalization; no claim is made that this ASCII spelling is itself the published terminology identifier.

This establishes a code-to-percentage definition only. It does not establish patient-level availability, a distinct specimen count, a disease-specific phenotype, specimen site, diagnosis date, baseline status, method equivalence, or a clinical risk group.
Do not infer MIPI-c or another score from a percentage code alone.
A true 0% code is a recorded value, not missingness. Out-of-range or nonnumeric suffixes are outside this verified family.
The explanatory PDF is a breast-cancer coding guide. The general code-family enumeration is verified independently in the full Patobank Ætiologi codebook.
Historical effective dates and the correctness of any particular exported clinical record were not audited. Existing aggregate rows and counts were not re-derived in this research task.

glossary.definition: Therapy administered at high dose; in the cited lymphoma context, used in connection with autologous stem cell transplantation.
glossary.locator: NCI lymphoma trial eligibility explicitly spells out high-dose therapy (HDT); dictionary defines high-dose chemotherapy.
glossary.caveat: HDT alone does not identify a regimen, prove transplantation occurred, or specify a dose. Do not silently expand every HDT field to high-dose chemotherapy without its source definition.

glossary.locator: NCI trial description explicitly spells out chemo-immunotherapy (CIT); dictionary supplies the general definition.
glossary.caveat: This is the intended oncology treatment expansion, not an export-specific codebook finding. CIT can have other meanings in other contexts; it does not identify a drug combination.

glossary.definition: A protein involved in the development and maturation of B cells; BTK inhibitors block its activity.
glossary.caveat: BTK names the protein. A BTK-inhibitor class label is not proof of a particular drug, exposure, mutation, or biomarker result.

glossary.expansion: Mantle Cell Lymphoma International Prognostic Index
glossary.definition: A prognostic index for mantle cell lymphoma incorporating age, ECOG performance status, LDH, and peripheral blood leukocyte count.
glossary.locator: Printed pages 4 and 6; prognostic tools paragraph on page 6.
glossary.caveat: A glossary definition does not establish which MIPI variant or calculation was used in an exported field. No score or risk group is derived here.

glossary.definition: A mantle cell lymphoma prognostic classification combining MIPI with the Ki-67 proliferation index.
glossary.locator: Printed page 7 explicitly describes Ki-67 score plus MIPI as MIPI-c.
glossary.caveat: Do not conflate MIPI-c with the distinct biologic MIPI (MIPI-b), or calculate it from a lone Ki-67 pathology code. No threshold or risk-group assignment is supplied here.

glossary.definition: In clinical data, commonly refers to the ECOG Performance Status Scale, which describes daily functioning, self-care, and physical activity.
glossary.caveat: ECOG is the originating group's abbreviation; label a score field as ECOG performance status when its source supports that meaning. No score conversion is inferred.

glossary.definition: Imaging that uses x-rays and computer processing to create detailed views of structures inside the body.
glossary.caveat: Use this expansion for imaging context. A modality or procedure code does not establish report-text or image-pixel availability.

glossary.definition: Imaging that uses a strong magnet, radio waves, and computer processing to depict internal structures.
glossary.caveat: A modality or procedure code does not establish report-text or image-pixel availability.

glossary.definition: Imaging using a radioactive tracer and a scanner to show where the tracer is taken up in the body.
glossary.caveat: The cited NCI entry describes radioactive glucose. PET alone does not identify a specific tracer, establish a positive finding, or imply image-pixel availability.

glossary.definition: A medical terminology family. For Danish pathology records, use the Danish pathology SNOMED / patoSnoMed classification identified by the source.
glossary.caveat: Do not treat Danish pathology SNOMED codes as interchangeable with SNOMED CT identifiers. Preserve the code system and version provenance.

glossary.definition: A classification that groups active drug substances by the organ or system affected and their therapeutic, pharmacological, and chemical properties.
glossary.caveat: An ATC code identifies a classification entry; it does not on its own establish administered dose, schedule, indication, or confirmed exposure.

glossary.definition: The collection of Danish clinical and administrative classifications maintained by the Danish Health Data Authority for documenting healthcare information and services.
glossary.caveat: Preserve the particular SKS code family and validity period. A generic SKS label alone does not identify the clinical meaning of a record.
